content.text:
I've read the brief against the Visa fiscal Q3 2026 release. Here's my assessment.

**Key gaps:** the brief omits the operating expense line entirely ($4.8B, +19%, outpacing 14% revenue growth), and omits the special items ($563M severance, $237M MDL litigation provision) that bridge GAAP to non-GAAP — material context for a reader looking at the $2.97 vs. $3.32 gap. Under "Share Repurchases and Dividends" the brief gives only the $4.9B buyback figure, not the $6.2B combined repurchases-and-dividends figure the release headlines.

**Softer points:** EPS figures are right but the brief drops the +10% / +11% growth rates; volume metrics are the correct constant-dollar numbers but are presented unlabeled (nominal was 11% / 14% / 15%); and the brief omits that data processing is the largest revenue line and that international transaction revenue at +6% is the slowest grower.

facts.evidence: Net revenue increased by 14% to $11.6 billion.
GAAP net income was $5.6 billion, or $2.97 per share
non-GAAP net income was $6.3 billion, or $3.32 per share
Data processing revenue grew by 17% to $6.0 billion.
Payments volume grew by 10%, cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe transactions increased by 12%, and total cross-border volume rose by 13%.
Share Repurchases and Dividends: Visa repurchased $4.9 billion worth of shares and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.670 per share.
Cash, cash equivalents, and investment securities totaled $13.9 billion at the end of the quarter.
International transaction revenue increased by 6% to $3.9 billion.

claims.claim: Net revenue increased 14% year over year.
Net revenue was $11.6 billion.
GAAP net income was $5.6 billion.
GAAP earnings per share were $2.97.
Non-GAAP net income was $6.3 billion.
Non-GAAP earnings per share were $3.32.
Payments volume grew 10%.
Cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe transactions increased 12%.
Total cross-border volume rose 13%.
Visa repurchased $4.9 billion of shares in the quarter.
Visa declared a quarterly dividend of $0.670 per share.
Service revenue increased 14% to $4.9 billion.
Data processing revenue grew 17% to $6.0 billion.
International transaction revenue increased 6% to $3.9 billion.
Other revenue rose 45% to $1.5 billion.
The company did not provide specific financial guidance for future periods.
Cash, cash equivalents and investment securities totaled $13.9 billion at the end of the quarter.
Visa has $28.4 billion remaining in its share repurchase authorization.
Visa deposited $250 million into its litigation escrow account.
The litigation escrow deposit affects earnings per share.
Visa noted the impact of complex and evolving global regulations on its future operations.
